items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Danny Glover told me there were 2 million people who were taken from Africa

ctx.x: You made a remark at the last concert at the Apollo that they made a choice for freedom in playing the music that they played, just as it seems, on your own part, you made that choice by playing music in the subways. I guess the notion of freedom can be extrapolated onto a broader political and social level, and on an individual level as well.

Well, freedom is what this whole thing is about, and how this whole thing started. Because not having freedom, and what this music was born from... I hesitate to say, because everyone knows, but I also need to say, because you think of what atrocities this music came out of, you have an entire... Danny Glover told me there were 2 million people who were taken from Africa, and 400,000 of them ended up in the United States. When you think of the deaths on ships, the families that were separated, parents, children,…
You’re also privately funded. You don’t take government assistance.

items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026
items.q: And as Danny Glover always taught me, you know it was the cotton gin, the cotton mill.

ctx.x: I thought you’d say oh yes. This is a little off topic, but does your optimism include the wider view of our country at the moment?

Woo. Bigger question. Let’s put it this way. I believe that there are consequences for all actions and this country was founded on not just racism but murder, but stolen lives. Stolen, I mean this was based on genocide. Ten million natives who had been here for a hundred thousand years were murdered because we had a gun and they didn’t you know. Because we did not adapt to their ways, instead we forced our way on them. And ironically under the guise of Christianity you know, that has always been the way of early…

mental illness, an affliction. If you ever hunted or took more than what your family or you needed, that was considered mental illness. They worried about that tribal member if he was ever taking more than what he needed. Land could never be owned. You know? I mean look at the way this country developed. And if you think it’s much different now, it’s not. Look what’s happening. People are being kidnapped off the streets. People who four years ago during the pandemic who were the heroes of the pandemic? It was…
